head.text: IDE write with the current logic (20 MHz, no wait states in practice)

signal.name: state
signal.data: S0 S1 S2 S3 S4 S5 S0 S1 S2 S3

foot.text: nIDE_WR = CPU_RW OR NOT IDE_WR_SIG. IDE_WR_SIG is armed by the first falling edge after the IDE1 select and sets on the next rising edge. With no wait states it only clears when R/W changes in the next cycle or the select goes away, so /IOW rises after /CS0 and after the data buffers are disabled. ATA latches on the rising edge of /IOW and needs CS and data held after it. IDE_WR_SIG_A and the wait-state clock only look at nIDE1_CSA/CSB, so IDE2 writes never produce /IOW.
